extracted.intended_audience: juvenile defense attorneys, legal scholars, policymakers, and judges interested in juvenile justice reform
extracted.subtask_description: A law-review note arguing for an expanded, youth-specific right to counsel in juvenile courts and recommending six concrete reforms to how children are represented. The piece grounds its recommendations in youths' developmental characteristics recognized in Eighth Amendment cases and in stories of deficient representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated youth defender's office
rubrics_metrics.description: Require each jurisdiction to have a dedicated youth defender's office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an office should provide specialized training and supervision tailored to representing children. The recommendation is grounded in the observation that children are distinct from adults and require counsel with specific skills and institutional support to avoid deficient representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized training and supervision for counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Defense counsel for youth must receive specialized training and ongoing supervision appropriate to juvenile practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should address developmental differences of youth, mitigation investigation, ethical issues unique to juvenile cases, and strategies for effective advocacy across adjudication and disposition. Supervision within a dedicated office helps ensure quality and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate common conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove or prevent common conflicts of interest that impair representation of children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Note argues that children frequently receive diminished advocacy because of structural and systemic conflicts (e.g., public defender resource constraints, overlapping responsibilities). Eliminating these conflicts is necessary to secure meaningful counsel for youth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory mitigation investigation and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Make mitigation mandatory in juvenile defense practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel should be required to investigate and present mitigating evidence about the child's background, developmental characteristics, and circumstances that bear on culpability and disposition, rather than leaving mitigation as discretionary or underdeveloped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guaranteed right to postdisposition advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Guarantee that youth have a right to advocacy after disposition (postdisposition advocacy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation should not end at sentencing or disposition; ongoing advocacy is necessary to address rehabilitation, reentry, compliance with conditions, and to challenge dispositional decisions when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic defense model for youth
rubrics_metrics.description: Move toward a holistic defense model for juvenile clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel should coordinate legal defense with social services, educational support, mental-health care, and family engagement to address the full needs of youth. A holistic model recognizes that legal outcomes are intertwined with social determinants and long-term wellbeing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Youth-specific ineffective-assistance-of-counsel standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a youth-specific standard for ineffective-assistance-of-counsel claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because children differ from adults (as recognized in Eighth Amendment jurisprudence), the standard for assessing counsel performance and prejudice in ineffective-assistance claims should reflect youths' developmental vulnerabilities and the different role counsel must play in juvenile cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation account for youth developmental differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation must account for the distinct characteristics of youth that the Court has recognized in Eighth Amendment cases (e.g., immaturity, susceptibility to outside influence, lack of true understanding of consequences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These characteristics justify additional protections and an expanded right to counsel; counsel's strategy, investigation, and communication should be tailored to developmental realities rather than treated the same as adult representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition that In re Gault is insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that In re Gault created a right to counsel for children that is weaker than for adults and thus insufficient to protect youth in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Gault did not foresee or remedy the ways in which youth require more expansive representation, reforms must go beyond simply ensuring a nominal right to counsel and should institute structural, procedural, and substantive changes to how juvenile defense is delivered.
